title: Arrow-target Cartesian fibration and pullback squares
statement: Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, coherent slices, mapping spaces and limiting cones from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and Cartesian edges and fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $C$ be a quasicategory in a fixed universe and assume that every cospan in $C$ has a pullback, meaning a limiting cone on that cospan. Put $\operatorname{Arr}(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ and let $t=\operatorname{ev}_1:\operatorname{Arr}(C)\to C$ be target evaluation. Then $t$ is a Cartesian fibration. An edge of $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$, viewed as a coherent square $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to C$, is $t$-Cartesian if and only if this square is a pullback. For $f:c'\to c$, Cartesian transport from the fiber at $c$ to the fiber at $c'$ sends $z\to c$ to $z\times_c c'\to c'$. This describes transport on entire coherent slice categories, including transformations and higher simplices. All pullbacks here are infinity-categorical pullbacks; no terminal object, presentability, or choice of pullback objects is assumed.

source.place: HTT Lemma 6.1.1.1, printed pp. 531-532 (PDF pp. 549-550); transport discussion immediately following it. Also GHN Remark 9.5. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategory theorem.

from.place: Proof paragraph 2, the presentable Cartesian-fibration construction before the finite-coefficient mapping-complex adjunction: GHN Proposition 9.12/9.16 and Corollary 9.17 identify the relative-cone presheaf subcategory with the Ind extension. Supporting GHN Definition 9.1, Lemma 9.4, Remark 9.5, Proposition 9.6 and Corollary 9.8, including the explicit fiber formula in the proof of Proposition 9.12. Supporting subargument: the arrow-target pullback-square criterion (GHN Remark 9.5).
